RagShortTexts: Claims over fugitives involve status, debt and local power.
Shelter or return can provoke disputes with kin and lords.

Variants.Content: A claimant pursuing someone who fled must explain the claim. Debt, marriage or mistreatment may enter the account. Hosts, kin and local authorities affect the outcome; a name or poor clothing does not settle status and duties.
Apprehending someone requires identification and guarantors. Mistakes turn debt disputes violent; feeding a prisoner also costs an escort whose claimant may not pay.
Authorities seek witnesses and hear both sides. Casual surrender discredits protection; arbitrary detention makes enemies. Relationships and original agreements determine appropriate handling.
Sheltering a fugitive shares food and lodging and exposes kin to questions. Hidden woodland provides neither seed nor winter housing; dependable neighbors matter.
